convoLines.text: "Do you dream about before? Or is it all — this — now?"
"Then it's not gone. Not really. Keep going back."
"Columbus, Ohio, always. Same dream: I'm walking home and the street keeps getting longer. I wake up tired, like I actually walked it."
"Still on what you dream about."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Good question." "I dreamed Duc was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Giulia grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Cesar is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I keep turning over the last thing Duc said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Duc. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
"I believe in breakfast. In people showing up. Small, provable things. The big beliefs all broke — the small ones held."
"Still on what you believe in."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Good question." "Duc owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I write everything down. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Cesar nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Me? Denver. I still dream in its weather — rain on a tin roof, that specific smell. I wake up here and for a second I'm furious at the sky for the swap."
"Still on where you're from. I hope that helps."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"Done talking." Noah turns away. "Come back when you're not playing detective."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"About that question — What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
A friend doesn't flinch at one sharp word. They let it go.
"Still on what scares you most. Rest when you can."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Duc is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Eric nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on your useful old-life skills."
"Forget it — go on, I'm listening. Not that it matters."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Since Duc died... I keep expecting to see Duc at the fire. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Cesar nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — What do you miss most? From before."
"Tell me — God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on what you miss most."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Eric nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"People here talk. What they say about you when you're not at the fire — that's the real answer to your question."
"A month ago I wouldn't have said any of this to you. That's not nothing."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on whether you still sing."
"I'll keep it to myself. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
Cesar nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You missed a real hot meal. Soup, you said — with a spoon. Any of that turn up?"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Cesar. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Go ahead — you've got my attention."
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took Caleb and Lena — Windfall, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I'm not okay. I'm saying it out loud so it's real: I'm not okay."
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
They shift over, making room. "Stay as long as you like."
"I keep going over it. Having someone here... it slows the spiral. Anyway — how are YOU doing?"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Giulia shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Still on that hard time."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Eric nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Giulia rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"That again?" Giulia sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Wild Ramps — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now."
Cesar has an edge today — something curdled.
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
"The cistern's nearly dry — 5 liters left. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that plant lesson."
Something in them stays shut, for now.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took me. Hide and Seek — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants. Just... be straight with me."
"My theory changes weekly. This week's: we're the control group. Somewhere there's a village that got instructions, and we're the ones they just... watched. Cheerful thought, right?"
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you think happened to us. That's the whole of it."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Giulia nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
Caleb looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"We went over this," Caleb says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Take care out there."
Caleb: "Don't just stand there — you've got opinions, right?"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. Caleb doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
They nod — and keep their distance, for now.
"Still on who you don't trust."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."

"I sharpen sticks down to nothing when I think about what it wants from us. It wants something. Everything wants something."

"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."

"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? At night I cry quietly so no one hears."
There's an ease between you now — the kind that takes weeks to build.
"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."
"The cistern's nearly dry — 2 liters left. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"2 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"About that plant lesson — yeah, we never did get back to that."
"About what they confided — yeah, we never did get back to that."
"I should go. You know where to find me."

"...Think about it? I'll be around."

"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 10 days back. Still on your mind? 'Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though.'"
"Someone has to answer it eventually. Everyone's doing the math on whether it'll be them."

"Still on what's been happening."

"Okay, I'm all ears."

"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."
"Right — go on, I'm listening."

"When it gets bad, I sleep in short shifts. It doesn't help, exactly. It gives my hands something to do while my head catches up."

recoverWide14: d30: That night, they bring Duc home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
burialWide14: d29: The village's quarrel was with Duc — and Duc is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d29: At the grave, Cesar, Eric, Ella and 3 more speak for Grace — "Duc trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.

d32: You bury Duc. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)

deathBeatLines: d29: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Duc Steele is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d29: 🕯️ Duc Steele is dead — contest. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d29: The village's quarrel was with Duc — and Duc is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.

echoSample: d32: "Good question." "I dreamed Duc was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
d32: "I keep turning over the last thing Duc said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d32: "The fire feels smaller without Duc. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
d32: "Good question." "Duc owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d36: "Last time things were different. They always are." "Duc is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
d36: "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Since Duc died... I keep expecting to see Duc at the fire. Stupid."

d32: The village raises a marker by the fire — Duc, day 32. contest. A place to stand.

lines: d29: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Duc Steele is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d29: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d29: 🕯️ Duc Steele is dead — contest. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d29: What Duc kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d29: "Duc's gone." Cesar looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Duc." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d29: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Grace blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d29: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d29: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d29: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d29: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d29: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d29: 📖 LEARNED: Keeping Morale (Level 1). People need small wins. Celebrate the little things. Despair is the real killer.
d29: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d29: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Duc Steele, 29 days. The mantle passes to Grace Obi.
d29: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Grace Obi, 43 — an ESL teacher. Her hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Scream Cheese.
d29: The village's quarrel was with Duc — and Duc is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d29: At the grave, Cesar, Eric, Ella and 3 more speak for Grace — "Duc trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d29: The fire knew Grace before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.
